perspective:
Gloria Bangura’s available information:

- I know Donald as a colleague who works part-time as a bartender at our company events. We’re not personally close; we mainly interact during those events.
- Over several events, I noticed he seemed distracted and lacking enthusiasm while serving drinks. At one busy event, I asked him if everything was okay with the job. He told me he wasn’t as into it as he used to be and that it felt repetitive.
- After that, I thought more about his situation and suspected his dissatisfaction might be connected to something bigger. I suggested he consider talking to a professional. He said he hadn’t really considered it and wasn’t sure it would help.
- After that conversation, I sensed a shift in his behavior toward me and worried he might have resented my suggestion, feeling I overstepped. I told him I only wanted to help because I cared and didn’t mean to make assumptions. He said he was a bit taken aback at first, but knew I meant well and that it was a lot to process.
- I felt relieved that the tension had eased and wanted to strengthen our working relationship. I invited him to collaborate on a new project, saying it could use his creative input. He accepted and said it sounded like a great opportunity.
- After working together, I saw that Donald made significant contributions and seemed more enthusiastic. I publicly acknowledged his work during a meeting, saying his efforts were crucial. He thanked me, said it meant a lot, and that he was glad to contribute and felt appreciated.
